payload.claim: `ready_task` rebuilds a resumed task's `CellOutcome` with `state` hardcoded to `READY_FOR_REVIEW` and `reviews` read back from the task's stored `findings.json` (line 1018), never re-deriving `review_state`. Before this diff that was safe because `anchored_blockers` only read the immutable `anchored` field; now it also matches any claim starting with `HOST_FILED`, a marker already written into old `findings.json` files by the pre-existing `survivor_finding`. So `saffron package` on a task that reached `READY_FOR_REVIEW` before this change, with no PR yet (PACKAGE having raised), and whose `findings.json` happens to carry an unanchored host-filed survivor, will now have `pr_body.render_pr_body` (via `anchored_blockers` at `saffron/report/pr_body.py:327`) render that survivor as a numbered 'Disagreement' with no rebuttal and no verdict (since `outcome.rebut_result` is `None`, there being no `rebuttal.json` for a task that never went through REBUT), while the task still ships as `READY_FOR_REVIEW` without ever having routed it to REBUT. The gates cannot see this because every test builds `findings.json` fresh under the current code; none exercises the old-data-read-by-new-selection-rule boundary that `saffron package`'s reconstruction path crosses.
